messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Interlingua, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Interlingua line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------|------------------|--------| | Vedi | imperative “see / behold” | Vide | “see / behold” | OK | | la | definite article, fem. sg. | le | “the” (definite article) | OK | | bestia | “the beast” (specific creature) | bestia | “beast” | OK | | per | preposition introducing cause | per | “because of / for” | OK | | cu' (cui) | relative pronoun “which” referring to *bestia* | le qual | “which” | OK | | io | 1st sg. pronoun, subject | io | “I” | OK | | mi | reflexive pronoun (self‑directed) | me | “myself” | OK | | volsi | past historic “turned” (self‑directed) | volve | “turned” | OK | | aiutami | 1st sg. imperative “help me” | Adjuta me | “help me” | OK | | da | preposition “against” (opposition) | contra | “against” | OK | | lei | 3rd sg. fem. pronoun “her” | illa | “her / she” | OK | | famoso | adjective “famous” (modifying *saggio*) | famose | “famous” | OK | | saggio | noun “sage” (vocative) | sapiente | “sage / wise one” | OK | | ch'ella (che ella) | subordinator “that / because” introducing cause | que | “that / because” | OK | | mi (again) | pronoun “me” as object of *fa* | me | “me” | OK | | fa | causative verb “makes” | face | “makes / causes” | OK | | tremar | infinitive “to tremble” | tremular | “to tremble” | OK | | le (article before *vene*) | definite article, fem. pl. | le | “the” | OK | | vene | plural “veins” | venas | “veins” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | e | “and” | OK | | i (article before *polsi*) | definite article, masc. pl. | le | “the” | OK | | polsi | plural “pulses” | pulsos | “pulses” | OK |
### Issues Detected - **None**. All source tokens are represented, translations respect the intended meanings, and no grammatical mismatches or unnecessary elements are present.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Interlingua script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Interlingua text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 88: - Original: Vide le bestia per le qual io me volve; - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- Line 89: - Original: Adjuta me contra illa famose sapiente, - Issue: GRAMMAR – adjective “famose” should be invariant “famoso” - Corrected: Adjuta me contra illa **famoso** sapiente,
- Line 90: - Original: que illa me face tremular le venas e le pulsos. - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
``` Vide le bestia per le qual io me volve; Adjuta me contra illa famoso sapiente, que illa me face tremular le venas e le pulsos. ```
